## 1. What Atlas Is

Atlas is a **multi-tenant SaaS education platform**: organizations ("Tenants") sign up, each Tenant can operate one or more Academies, each Academy runs Course Management + Student Learning + Instructor Operations + Community features (Announcements/Blog/Forum), each Academy can configure and publish its own public marketing website (Theme Engine + Page Composer + CMS + SEO + a real public runtime), and Atlas itself (the "Platform") layers subscriptions/billing, provisioning, and (partially) platform-wide administration on top.

This repository is **frontend only**. Every prompt from Prompt 1 onward has treated the backend as abstract/undocumented-but-contracted: real services, real hooks, real types, real Zod validation, real loading/error/empty states — calling a real (currently non-existent) backend through one real API client. Nothing in the "Complete" domains (§8) fakes success, fakes latency, or fakes data. Some of the *oldest* code (Prompt 3 Part A) does — that is the central finding of Prompt 12 (§9) and the reason this handoff exists.

Student-facing experience on top of Academy + Course: discovery (a new flat, cross-academy `discoverCourses`/`discoverCourse` pair — the *only* new endpoint shape needed since everything else reused Part 3), enrollment, curriculum navigation, lesson consumption, progress, quizzes, assignments, completion/certificate-eligibility state (no real certificate generation). Established: a **third service-tree pattern** — Student Learning gets its own flat `courses/:courseId/...` tree, separate from Course Management's academy-scoped tree, because a student reaches a course by id alone (from their own enrollment), never via an academy id in the URL. Every query key embeds the current student's id (from `useAuth().user.id`, never a parameter — removing an entire class of possible cross-student leakage by construction). ### Prompt 8 — Atlas Provisioning + Academy Lifecycle (VERIFIED)
The orchestration domain: Tenant → Academy → Theme → Branding → Subdomain → Domain → Provisioning → Ready. A real, idempotent, resumable state machine — `ProvisioningRequest` carries both a coarse 12-value `ProvisioningStatus` and a real `steps[]` array (7 steps × pending/running/completed/failed/skipped), so retry logic reads step completion directly rather than inferring it. The `tenant` and `theme` steps are **observability-only** — Prompt 8 does not create Tenants (existing registration flow owns that) and does not implement a Theme Engine (Prompt 9 owns that); both render `'skipped'` until their owning system exists. `retryProvisioning` deliberately covers both "retry" and "resume" as one contract. `SubdomainAllocation`/`DomainConnection` model **display state only** — no real DNS/SSL — this is the exact type vocabulary Prompt 11 later reused verbatim rather than duplicating. The `'ready'` success state offers only "Go to Academy Dashboard," never "Visit Website," because Prompt 8 has no way to know whether a public website exists (it didn't yet).

The multi-tenant Theme Engine and Page Composer for an Academy's public website, on Prompt 3B/3C's Academy/Course foundation. **Naming-collision precedent #3, the largest**: discovered a pre-existing, unrelated dashboard light/dark `Theme`/`ThemePreference`/`ThemeProvider` system and prefixed every new type/file `Website*`, never bare `Theme*` — this rule must never be violated. ### Prompt 11 — Atlas Public Website Runtime + Full Website CMS + Domain/Cloudflare Readiness (VERIFIED — implemented in this session)
Four objectives, all extending 9/10, never rewriting them:
- **(A) CMS gap-closure**: audited every Section Registry config against a worked example; found `WebsiteCta.url` had been a typed field with **zero reachable UI** since Prompt 9 (`CtaFieldEditor` only ever exposed a page picker). Fixed additively: `HeroSectionConfig.eyebrow`/`imageAlt`, `AboutSectionConfig.imageAlt`, `GalleryImage.imageAlt`, `TestimonialItem.avatarAlt`, `WebsiteCta.courseId`; rebuilt `CtaFieldEditor` with a real Link Type selector (Page/External URL/Course); built `isSafeExternalUrl` (rejects `javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:`/`file:`); the identical Link Type fix was also applied to the Header CTA editor once the same gap was found there. **Deliberately excluded**: Blog Post/Announcement as CTA link targets (neither has a public rendering surface), `mobileImage`/`backgroundImage` (no responsive art-direction infrastructure exists anywhere in Atlas).
- **(B) Public website runtime**: `PublicWebsiteRouter`, mounted by `AppRouter` **instead of** (never alongside) the normal dashboard/auth/marketing tree, based on a new pure function `resolvePublicWebsiteContext`. Returns `{mode:'atlas-app'}` unconditionally whenever `ENV.platformBaseDomain` is unset (true in every environment today) — this is the literal mechanism proving the app works safely with no real Atlas domain. `PublicWebsiteService` is a deliberate **third, separate** service tree (no session; Academy identity comes FROM the hostname via `resolveHostname`, `useParams` is never used in this feature). Reuses the exact `WebsiteRenderer`/`CourseDetailsTemplate` via a new optional `WebsiteLinkRenderer` render-seam (absent everywhere in the dashboard, real navigation only in the public runtime).
- **(C) SEO runtime**: `useDocumentSeo`, hand-rolled `document.head` management (no head-library exists in this stack), JSON-LD emitted via `document.createElement('script').textContent = JSON.stringify(...)` — **zero `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere**, strictly safer than the pattern the spec itself cautioned about. `robots.txt`/`sitemap.xml` show real generated content at those routes but are explicitly documented as **not** real `Content-Type: text/plain` HTTP serving — a pure SPA cannot control response headers for an arbitrary path; that is a future Cloudflare Worker/edge layer's job.
- **(D) Domain/DNS/SSL/CDN/Cloudflare readiness**: reuses Prompt 8's `DomainStatus`/`DomainConnection`/`SubdomainAllocation` verbatim (no duplicate state machine). New: `SslStatus`/`CdnStatus`/`InfrastructureProviderStatus` (every status defaults to "not configured"; `connected` never assumed `true`). `WebsiteDomainTab` (Academy) + `PlatformDomainSettingsPage` (Platform Owner, mirrors `PlatformTrialPolicyPage` exactly, `requiredRoles: ['platform_owner']`, zero new permission strings). **No fake Cloudflare API, no fake DNS/SSL/CDN success, ever.**

`@features/website` was given its first root public barrel (`index.ts`), deliberately curated (renderer + pure utils only), since Prompt 11's public runtime was the first genuinely external cross-feature consumer of it.

## 5. Current Architecture

**Stack** (from `package.json`, `Reports/📘 Atlas AI Constitution.md` Chapter 2): React 18 + TypeScript, Vite + `@vitejs/plugin-react-swc`, React Router v6, Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui primitives, TanStack Query, React Hook Form + Zod, `react-i18next` (EN/AR, LTR/RTL), `lucide-react` icons, axios (wrapped, never called directly).

**Layered pattern, mandatory for every domain:**
```
Component → Hook (useApiQuery/useApiMutation) → Service (extends BaseService) → apiClient → backend (abstract)
```
`src/services/base.service.ts` — every service extends this; `protected readonly resource` + `this.path(...segments)`. `src/services/api/api-client.ts` — the one HTTP entry point; `src/services/api/http-client.ts` — attaches the auth token "if available" (never required — this is how the public website runtime works unauthenticated through the *same* client, with no second HTTP client ever built).

**Query keys** (`src/services/query/query-keys.ts`) — one factory per domain, `QUERY_KEY_ROOTS` centralizes root arrays. Every domain's keys embed their scope id directly (`organizationId` for Tenant-scoped, `academyId` for Academy-scoped, `studentId`/current-user-id for Student-scoped, hostname/academyId for public-runtime-scoped) — this is how cross-scope cache leakage is prevented structurally, not by convention.

**Feature directories** (`src/features/<name>/`): `academy`, `analytics`, `announcements`, `auth`, `billing` (holds BOTH the real Prompt 7 payment pages AND the legacy Prompt 3A shell, in one directory — see §9), `blog`, `course`, `dashboard`, `domain` (Prompt 11), `forum`, `home`, `instructor`, `learning`, `notifications`, `platform`, `profile`, `provisioning`, `public-website` (Prompt 11), `search`, `settings`, `system`, `tenant`, `website` (Prompts 9–11).

**Public feature barrels** (`src/features/<name>/index.ts`, only where it exists — used by `no-restricted-imports` to allow bare `@features/<name>` cross-feature imports, never deep `@features/<name>/<path>`): confirmed present for `course`, `blog`, `tenant`, `domain`, `public-website`, `website` (the last added in Prompt 11 specifically, and deliberately curated, not a blanket `export *`).

**Routing**: `src/app/routes/route-paths.ts` (`PUBLIC_ROUTES`/`AUTH_ROUTES`/`DASHBOARD_ROUTES`/`SYSTEM_ROUTES`), `src/app/routes/AppRouter.tsx` (one `<Routes>` tree for the authenticated app, lazy-loaded pages; **plus**, since Prompt 11, a top-level hostname branch that renders `PublicWebsiteRouter` instead of that tree entirely — see §13), `src/app/routes/guards/` (`RouteGuard`, fail-closed).

**Navigation**: `src/app/navigation/navigation.config.ts` — declarative sections/items, each with `requiresAuth`/`requiredPermissions`/`requiredRoles`. This file is the actual, current, complete map of what's reachable in the dashboard — read it directly rather than trusting a prose description (including this one).

**Authorization**: `src/services/identity/authorization.service.ts` — `hasPermission`/`hasAllPermissions`/`hasAnyPermission`, operating on flat `readonly string[]` permission arrays on `CurrentUser`/`OrganizationContext` (see §8/§15 — there is no `Role`/`Permission` entity type anywhere in `src/types`).

**Localization**: `src/localization/resources/{en,ar}/<namespace>.json`, registered in `src/localization/resources/index.ts` and `src/types/localization.types.ts`'s `TRANSLATION_NAMESPACES`. Every prompt that added a namespace verified EN/AR key-count parity programmatically before finishing (see §16).

**Website/CMS/Public-Runtime architecture**: `src/features/website/` (themes, renderer, sections, CMS content, SEO utils, domain UI tab), `src/features/domain/` (Academy + Platform domain readiness), `src/features/public-website/` (hostname resolution, public service/hooks, the public route tree) — see §13/§14 for full detail.

## 6. Non-Negotiable Architectural Rules

These are established, verified, and must not be violated by any future session:

1. **Layering is mandatory**: Component → Hook → Service → `apiClient`. No direct `fetch`/`axios` call from a page or component, ever, in any domain claiming to be real.
2. **No fake backend, no fake data, no fake latency.** No `setTimeout`/`setInterval` standing in for real async work. No hardcoded arrays presented as if they were an API response. No toast/success state shown without a real mutation behind it. *(This exact rule was violated in Prompt 3A's Search and Settings — that is a confirmed historical defect, not a sanctioned exception; see §18.)*
3. **No hardcoded business-rule values** (trial days, prices, plan behavior, permission strings invented ad hoc). Where a number must exist before a backend does, it lives in one named constant, consumed as query `initialData` marked stale, never as an unconditional literal.
4. **Fail-closed authorization.** `RouteGuard` must default to denying access; every dashboard route must explicitly set `requireAuthentication` (a real regression happened once in Prompt 3B and was fixed — this rule exists because of that incident, and grep-verification of "N/N RouteGuards set requireAuthentication" is standing practice every prompt since).
5. **Strict scope isolation.** Tenant-scoped data keys on `organizationId`; Academy-scoped data keys on `academyId`; Student-scoped data keys on the current user's own id (never a parameter); Public-runtime data keys on hostname/academyId resolved server-side, never trusted from a route param. No domain may read another scope's cache by construction.
6. **No duplicate infrastructure.** Before building a new service/hook/type/upload mechanism/renderer/authorization system, search the repository for an existing one. This rule has been followed literally in every prompt (e.g., `useFilePicker`+base64 reused eleven times rather than building a Media Library — see §9/§18 for why that specific reuse is now itself flagged as insufficient at scale).
7. **Naming-collision discipline.** Before introducing a new type/feature name, grep for it. Three real collisions were found and resolved this way (`billing`/`Billing*` legacy feature, dashboard `Theme*` system, `BreadcrumbItem` in `navigation.types.ts`). `Website*` prefix convention must be preserved for anything in the website/theme domain.
8. **Content vs. presentation separation** (website/CMS domain): sections reference course/CMS-entry ids, never copy their data. Theme switching must never alter page content.
9. **Draft vs. published is absolute** (website/CMS/public-runtime domain): the public runtime renders ONLY published, visible, non-archived content. Publishing is always one explicit, backend-confirmed action; nothing auto-publishes; nothing is optimistically marked published before the backend confirms.
10. **No fake infrastructure status** (domain/SSL/CDN domain): every status defaults to "not configured"; nothing is marked active/connected/verified by the frontend itself.
11. **URL safety.** Any URL a tenant can type and that later becomes a rendered `href` must pass `isSafeExternalUrl` (`src/features/website/utils/url-safety.utils.ts`) — rejects `javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:`/`file:`.
12. **No client-side secrets.** Infrastructure/provider credentials (Cloudflare or otherwise) must never be read by, stored in, or exposed to the frontend. `InfrastructureProviderStatus` carries only a boolean.
13. **EN/AR parity is verified programmatically**, not eyeballed, every time a namespace changes.
14. **State completeness**: every domain claiming to be real must implement the full matrix in §17 — a happy-path-only UI is not "done."
15. **Don't redesign working (Complete, §8) domains.** Extend them. The one time a signature was narrowed (`buildOrganizationJsonLd`/`buildCourseJsonLd` in Prompt 11), it was done in a way that kept every existing call site compiling unchanged.

## 11. Recommended Order (Not A Prompt — A Recommendation)

Derived directly from §7/§9's priorities:

1. **P0 — Roles & Permissions type contract.** Every other Control Plane console (§12) needs to know what it's gating against; building consoles before this exists risks rework.
2. **P0 — Organization Admin Console, Academy Global Console, User Directory.** These three are structurally similar (list/search/filter/detail over a cross-tenant entity) and likely share patterns.
3. **P0 — Notifications, Search, Settings, Platform Dashboard, Analytics.** Replace the five shells with real services/hooks/data. Search and Settings contain the confirmed anti-pattern violations (§18) and should be prioritized within this group.
4. **P1 — Audit Log**, since Platform Dashboard's "recent activity" and any future admin action logging depend on it.
5. **P1 — Support Operations, Plan/Add-on Administration, Media Library, legacy Billing resolution.**
6. **P2 — Wire existing `resolveCourseSeo`/`resolveBlogPostSeo` into a live panel; Feature Flags admin UI if/when needed.**
7. **Only then** should broad backend implementation begin against the domains completed in steps 1–6, in parallel with backend work already safe to start today against the 9 Complete domains (§8A).

## 13. Public Website Runtime

Full detail in `Reports/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s Prompt 11 section ("Atlas Public Website Runtime + Full Website CMS + Domain/Cloudflare Readiness"); summarized here for continuity.

**Why architecturally separate from the dashboard**: an anonymous public visitor has no session, and the Academy being served must be resolved from the *hostname*, not any client-supplied id — this is a security-sensitive boundary (§15). `AppRouter` (`src/app/routes/AppRouter.tsx`) calls `resolvePublicWebsiteContext` (`src/features/public-website/utils/hostname-resolution.utils.ts`) exactly once, before choosing which `<Routes>` tree to render, and mounts `PublicWebsiteRouter` **instead of**, never alongside, the dashboard/auth/marketing tree — there is no path collision with Atlas's own `/` marketing route because only one tree is ever mounted per pageview.

**Resolution chain**: hostname → `resolvePublicWebsiteContext` (pure, testable — `{mode:'atlas-app'}` unconditionally when `ENV.platformBaseDomain` is unset) → `PublicWebsiteService.resolveHostname` (real backend call, returns `HostnameResolution | null`) → `academyId` → `usePublicWebsiteData` (composes hostname + published config + published pages into one exhaustive state: `loading | not-found | unavailable | unpublished | ready`) → `PublicWebsitePage` renders the resolved `WebsitePage` through the **same** `WebsiteRenderer`/`CourseDetailsTemplate` the dashboard preview uses, via `resolvePathToPage` (path → page, excludes hidden pages always) → SEO via `useDocumentSeo` + the Page Override → Website Global → Atlas System Fallback hierarchy (`resolvePageSeo`, Prompt 10, unchanged) → structured data via pure builders + real `document.head` DOM APIs (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`) → `robots.txt`/`sitemap.xml` shown as generated content at those routes (not real HTTP serving — see §6 rule 9/§18).

**Key files**: `src/features/public-website/PublicWebsiteRouter.tsx`, `src/features/public-website/services/PublicWebsiteService.ts`, `src/features/public-website/hooks/{usePublicWebsiteData,useDocumentSeo,useResolveHostname,usePublishedWebsite,usePublishedPages,usePublishedPage}.ts`, `src/features/public-website/utils/{hostname-resolution,page-resolution,robots-sitemap}.utils.ts`, `src/features/public-website/components/{PublicWebsitePage,PublicWebsiteStatus,PublicWebsiteRobotsRoute,PublicWebsiteSitemapRoute}.tsx`.

**Dev-only testing path**: `?__atlas_academy_preview=<slug>` query param, active only when `ENV.isDevelopment` — never relevant once a real domain routes real traffic.

## 15. Security / Authorization Model

- `RouteGuard` (`src/app/routes/guards/`) — fail-closed; every dashboard route explicitly sets `requireAuthentication` (grep-verified count as of Prompt 11: 64/64).
- Permission checks: `usePermissions()`/`AuthorizationService.hasPermission` — flat string-array membership, both route-level (`requiredPermissions`) and Platform-Owner-role-level (`requiredRoles: ['platform_owner']`) gates exist and are structurally distinct (a permission string can never imply the Platform Owner role).
- **No `Role`/`Permission` entity type exists** — this is a confirmed gap (§7/§9), not a hidden feature to discover.
- Scope isolation: organization/academy/student/hostname id embedded directly in every relevant query key (§6 rule 5); never inferred from a route param where a trusted source (`useAuth()`, `resolveHostname`) exists.
- Public-runtime hostname resolution is explicitly treated as security-sensitive: Academy identity comes only from `resolveHostname`'s backend response; `useParams` is never used anywhere in `@features/public-website` (grep-verified).
- URL safety: `isSafeExternalUrl` (§6 rule 11) is the one and only URL-scheme validator; reused, never reimplemented per field.
- No client-side secrets: confirmed by grep for Cloudflare-credential-shaped strings across the repository — none found. `InfrastructureProviderStatus.connected` is the only signal exposed, a boolean.
- No card data (`cardNumber`/`cvv`/`expiry`) is ever collected or stored in the frontend (Prompt 7 rule, still true).
- **A future session must not weaken any of the above** to make a new feature "easier" — e.g., must not read `academyId` from a route param in the public runtime, must not add a permission-string check without a corresponding real permission the backend will also enforce, must not add a URL field without wiring it through `isSafeExternalUrl`.

## 16. Localization

`react-i18next`, EN + AR, LTR + RTL. Resource files: `src/localization/resources/{en,ar}/<namespace>.json`, registered in `src/localization/resources/index.ts` and `TRANSLATION_NAMESPACES` (`src/types/localization.types.ts`). Current namespaces include (non-exhaustive, check the files directly for the current list): `common`, `navigation`, `validation`, `academy`, `course`, `learning`, `instructor`, `announcements`, `blog`, `forum`, `tenant`, `payments`, `provisioning`, `website`, `analytics`, `platform`, `settings`, `notifications`, `search`, `billing` (legacy).

**Rule for adding new keys**: add to both `en/<ns>.json` and `ar/<ns>.json` in the same edit; verify parity programmatically (a small Node script comparing flattened key sets — every prompt from 9–11 did this and reported an exact N/N count before finishing). Never leave one language with more/fewer keys than the other. Real tenant-authored content (course titles, website page content, CMS entries) is **not** a translation key — only Atlas's own UI chrome is.

---

## 17. State Matrix

A screen is not "done" because its happy path renders. Every domain claiming to be real must handle: loading, empty, error, retry, permission-denied, saving, deleting, uploading, publishing/unpublishing, unsaved-changes-protection (where applicable), pagination, search, filtering, sorting (where applicable) — across mobile/tablet/desktop, RTL/LTR, light/dark mode, with real EN/AR text throughout. The 9 Complete domains (§7) all satisfy this. The 5 UI-shell domains fail it structurally — not because the state components are missing, but because there is no request whose failure/success those states would represent.

---

## 18. Known Anti-Patterns — Must Never Return

Confirmed present in the repository today (Prompt 3A legacy code, never fixed by any later prompt because none of them were scoped to touch it):

1. **Fake `setTimeout`-as-latency** — `SearchPage.tsx`: `await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 300))`.
2. **Mock array presented as an API response** — `SearchPage.tsx`'s hardcoded 6-item `mockResults`, with a code comment admitting it: `// Mock search function - in real implementation, this would call a search service`.
3. **Fake success toast with no mutation** — `GeneralSettings.tsx`'s submit handler calls `toast({...})` directly, with no service call preceding it.
4. **Hardcoded business metric** — `PlatformMetrics.tsx`'s `metrics` array: `{ label: "systemHealth", value: 100 }` etc., literal, not fetched.
5. **Hardcoded status badge** — `BillingPage.tsx`'s `<Badge>{t('billing:status.active')}</Badge>`, unconditional.
6. **Decorative, non-functional controls** — `SecuritySettings.tsx`/`NotificationSettings.tsx`'s `<Switch>` components with no `onCheckedChange`.
7. **Duplicated/confusing surfaces for the same concept** — three "billing" entry points in nav (legacy shell, real Tenant Billing, real Payment Review) with no disambiguation for a user.

**Everywhere else in the codebase**, these patterns were caught and prevented at design time (every prompt from 4 onward explicitly grepped for `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`console.log`/mock arrays as part of its own CTO audit before declaring completion). Do not introduce any of the above seven patterns in new code, and treat any of the five UI-shell domains as needing a full rebuild of their data layer, not a patch.
